newsitem.title: Indonesia: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - Oct 4.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - Oct 4.

text.p: The following is a summary of major Indonesian political and business stories in leading newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Jakarta. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not guarantee their accuracy. Telephone: (6221) 384-6364. Fax: (6221) 344-8404.

Abdurrahman Wahid, leader of the 30-million strong muslim organisation Nahdlatul Ulama, has appealed to the ousted leader of the Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI) Megawati Sukarnoputri to drop her lawsuit against the government as it is producing no result. Megawati took the government to court for backing a congress in June which ousted her as the party leader.

Indonesia says it will back Boutros Boutros-Ghali in his bid to be reappointed as U.N. Secretary-General for a second five-year term. Foreign Minister Ali Alatas said the possibility of a veto on Boutros-Ghali's candidature by the United States could not be ruled out.
Indonesian property company PT Dharmala Intiland has secured a 40 billion rupiah syndicated loan to build a new office block in the East Java city of Surabaya.
Indonesian interest rates are expected to remain high even though inflation is below eight percent, the Center for Strategic International Studies said on Thursday.

The European Union (EU) has asked for consultation with the World Trade Organisation (WTO) over Indonesia's national car. The controversial Timor national car has been given special tax and tariff breaks by the Indonesian government which Japan, the United States and the EU say break WTO rules.
